subject: ventures/tow-truck-rate-calculator
professional: an independent tow-company owner or dispatcher who prices jobs and keeps a posted rate sheet, with a small-fleet bookkeeper checking the cost allocation

evidence.correctness: Ran node --test '*.test.mjs' in ventures/tow-truck-rate-calculator: 24 pass, 0 fail. Wrote an independent Python implementation of the README formulas (scratchpad/ind.py) and compared four unlike scenarios (default, heavy winch job, deadhead-dominated loss, storage-only) to rateOutcome output via node: cost, revenue, profit and target price agree to 4 decimals in all four. The default per-mile cost (0.75) sits next to the IRS 76 c/mile all-in car rate (irs.gov, fetched 2026-11-10); it is variable-only and editable, but light for a wrecker. Arithmetic is right; the remaining doubt is the defaults, scored under domain.
evidence.completeness: Every claimed feature works: true cost with deadhead, margin, break-even, target price, ranked levers, break-even per-mile rate, three surcharges, storage, validation. All 22 README inputs have a labelled field (page.test.mjs passes). The README states what is not covered (tolls, gate/impound fees, motor-club payouts, taxes, rate caps). No stubs or dead links found in the source. Admin, search and cleanup fees that Florida 713.78(20) expects on a rate sheet are not modelled, a disclosed scope limit.
evidence.verification: Ran node --test '*.test.mjs': 24 pass. Seeded 7 mutations in calc.mjs, each reverted (git diff clean afterwards): included-miles ignored, markup instead of margin, deadhead dropped, margin cap 95->100, insurance dropped, winch fee dropped were each caught; the finding threshold margin < target changed to margin <= target-0.05 survived because tests use 30% and 80% targets far from the boundary. 6 of 7 caught; hand-computed expected values (not snapshots) in the tests.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (124 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs. Pure functions, one validate() path, no copied engine, formulas documented in the header, round2 only on lever gains. Defects: all-zero job returns 'Margin n/a meets your target' as info; fractional storage days accepted silently; no upper bound on miles (1e9 miles gives a 2 billion dollar cost without warning). Minor.
evidence.claims: README and index.html carry the no-warranty disclaimer, the 'many states regulate tow rates, check yours' caveat, privacy statement and a Not modelled list; page.test.mjs asserts these and the $81.00 worked example. No performance, usage or savings claim is made; VENTURE.yaml marks the hypothesis untested. llms.txt links the old github.io host, which the Pages build rewrites, so not counted as a defect.
evidence.fitness: A solo operator can type their own costs and get a margin and a floor price in a few minutes, which is the stated job. A dispatcher quoting real calls would also need a minimum charge, a portal-to-portal (garage-to-garage) mileage option, gate/admin/after-hours-hour-of-day rules and a comparison to the local posted cap; none is modelled, so the output is a cost floor, not a quotable rate sheet.
evidence.domain: Method is fully-allocated hourly plus per-mile costing with deadhead included, a standard approach and well explained. Departures a tow owner or bookkeeper would raise: fixed costs spread only over billable hours the user guesses (150 default) with no utilisation or idle-time input; no depreciation or driver burden (payroll tax, workers comp, usually 20 to 40% on top of wage) in the defaults; wear default $0.25/mile is light for a heavy wrecker; the storage cost model has no lot overhead; and no rate-cap check (Florida 713.78 says charges may not exceed county or municipal maximum rates). All disclosed in the page, but the defaults are uncited.

defects.what: No minimum charge, garage-to-garage mileage, admin/gate/cleanup fee lines or a cap check, so the output is a cost floor and cannot become a posted rate sheet (Florida 713.78(20) lists these items)
Default wear and driver cost are uncited and light for a heavy wrecker (no payroll burden, $0.25/mile); users who leave defaults understate cost
Seeded change to the under-target finding threshold leaves all 24 tests green; no test near the margin == target boundary
All-zero job reports 'Margin n/a meets your target' instead of asking for data; absurd mileage (1e9) accepted without a warning

verdict: Tow Truck Rate Calculator is a small, correct and honestly scoped cost-plus pricing calculator. Four independent scenarios match a separately written implementation to four decimals, 24 tests pass, and 6 of 7 seeded mutations were caught (the survivor is the margin-vs-target threshold). Claims are backed and the disclaimer and rate-cap caveat are present. It meets the bar on correctness, claims and verification (all 3) with a median of 3, but only as a cost floor: fitness and domain are 2 because it has no minimum charge, garage-to-garage mileage, ancillary fee lines or cap comparison, and its defaults (wear, payroll burden) are uncited and light for a wrecker.
